subject: Copperfield: Checkout 502/latency spike — request for cross-region failover

From: Tara Nunez <ops@copperfieldretail.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: Checkout failures & latency spike (us-west)

Steph —

We started seeing a large spike in 502s and tokenization timeouts hitting our checkout microflow around 08:45 PDT. The spike correlates with increased latency across the us-west AZ cluster; impacting ~18% of checkout attempts and causing several customer-facing payment failures. We attached a short sample of recent 502 traces and the traffic metrics for the last two hours.

Key impact:
- 502 / 5xx errors increased from ~0.05% baseline to 3.7% between 08:45–09:05 PT.
- Median latency for the checkout path rose from 120ms to 880ms.
- Peak QPS during spike ~2.1x normal.

We need immediate mitigation — can you confirm if Redwood can steer traffic away from us-west to us-east while you triage? We are on a high-volume sale window and this is causing lost transactions. Please mark this P0.

Attachments: copperfield-502-sample-logs.txt, traffic-metrics-20280613.csv

Thanks,
Tara Nunez
Platform Lead, Copperfield Retail
ops@copperfieldretail.com

Subject: Internal: Copperfield P0 — triage & mitigation plan

Team —

Summary: Copperfield (CF-2026-EXP-0942) reporting ~3.7% 5xx + median checkout latency ~880ms in us-west AZ since ~08:45 PT. Peak QPS ~2.1x baseline. They are in a high-volume window and request immediate mitigation (traffic steering).

Immediate asks:
1) Sean / Marissa: Please confirm whether we can do a staged steering (25/60/100) to us-east cluster without requiring additional legal/data-residency checks (they are US-only customer, quick check). We should also prepare cache warm-up and KV prefetch notes.
2) Hannah: Hold readiness for a rollback and watch for KVCACHE cold-start amplification. Estimate time-to-warm: 10–18 minutes for hot models.
3) Ops: Prepare comms for Copperfield execs, and draft the MAP + one-time credit proposal (we'll attach).

Proposed short plan (execute after customer approval):
- T+0: Canary 25% traffic -> us-east (5 min observation window + health checks).
- T+5: If green, shift to 60% (10 min observation window).
- T+15: Full shift to 100% if green; monitor error-rate and tail latency.
- If error-rate rises >1% or payment failures persist, revert to original routing and open infra escalation.

I’ll message Tara to get approval, and keep legal/finance on standby for credit discussion. CC’ing you all.

-Steph

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-13T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Copperfield P0 — triage & mitigation plan

We can run the staged steer. Notes from infra:
- Routing: we can configure weighted routing at the edge (service router) immediately. We’ll push 25% in ~2 minutes and monitor.
- Cache warm-up: expect initial tokenization latency to remain high for early requests until KVCACHE warms; recommend adding a lightweight prefix cache and increasing prefetch concurrency for their checkout model during the canary.
- Risk: if backpressure exists in downstream payment adapters, steering may surface mismatches; confirm their payment provider endpoints are reachable from us-east.

Operational timeline:
- T+2m: push 25% (health-checks: 502 rate, median latency, payment success rate).
- T+8m: evaluate; if all health metrics within thresholds, push 60%.
- T+20m: target 100% if no regressions.

I’ll be on the bridge and will post live metrics to the channel. If we get any CPU/IO pressure on the us-east pool, we’ll cap at 60% and engage deeper infra.

Sean
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
